name: How much does a pool renovation cost in Los Angeles for just tile, coping, and plaster?

mainEntity.name: How much should I budget for a pool renovation in Los Angeles if I only replace the tile, coping, and plaster?
mainEntity.text: How much should I budget for a pool renovation in Los Angeles if I only replace the tile, coping, and plaster?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the goal is a clean cosmetic refresh, a pool renovation that includes plaster, waterline tile, and coping is usually the most common mid-scope project. In Los Angeles, pricing can vary widely based on pool size, finish type, demolition needs, and whether any hidden damage is found once the old surface is removed. A smaller pool with standard materials may stay near the low end, while larger pools, custom tile, natural stone coping, or premium finishes can push the project much higher. The biggest budget surprises usually come from cracked shell repair, deck tie-ins, leak repair, or outdated plumbing discovered during demolition. For the most accurate estimate, ask contractors to separate surface work, structural repairs, and equipment upgrades so you can compare apples to apples. If the goal is resale value or a luxury upgrade, spending more on finish quality and clean detailing usually creates a bigger visual impact than adding features first.
acceptedAnswer.description: A basic pool renovation in Los Angeles that includes replastering, waterline tile, and coping often falls in the mid five-figure range, with smaller resurfacing-only jobs starting lower and premium finishes costing more. Final price depends on pool size, surface condition, access, and whether plumbing or equipment upgrades are added.
